subtitle: sc-compose bounded adversarial-fuzzing campaign -- verification re-run against the fixed report-generation pipeline (PR #165, baseline 749a3e0)

recommendations_html:
• File and prioritize a fix for GH #169 (quadratic-time var-file recursion-depth latency in crates/sc-compose/src/var_file.rs::parse_var_file_contents) as a genuine performance-NFR gap.
  • Resolve the numeric-fidelity decision behind GH #170 (silent lossy-f64 downgrade of out-of-u64-range JSON integers) and record it as an ADR once decided.
  • Leave GH #167 (loop.* misclassified as undeclared under --strict) and GH #168 (var-file path confinement gap) with their existing owners; both are out of scope for PR #165 and were only reconfirmed, not newly introduced.
  • Document the --var-file/--var last-loaded-wins precedence in docs/requirements.md FR-2 (boundary-probe FUZZ-B01); this is intentional, deterministic behavior that only needs documentation, not a code change.
  • No action needed on PR #165 itself: differential-probe's 20/20 clean baseline-vs-head comparison confirms the diff is behavior-neutral for the rendering engine (docs/examples/skill-template files only, zero changes under crates/ or bindings/).

sections.title: Worker: shape-probe
sections.summary: 16/20 passed. GH #169 confirmed_bug (quadratic-time recursion-depth latency). GH #170 inconclusive (silent lossy-f64 bignum precision loss).
sections.body_html:
Target: var-file · Seed 261 · Iterations 20 · Passed 16 · Failed/flagged 4 · Result FAIL.

Two depth-cap-latency cases (depth 8000 = 0.697s, depth 16000 = 2.653s, scaling to ~25.6s at depth 50000) show O(depth^2) wall-time growth before sc-compose rejects deeply-nested var-file input via ERR_CONFIG_PARSE: recursion limit exceeded, in crates/sc-compose/src/var_file.rs::parse_var_file_contents's serde_yaml fallback path. Reproduced 3/3 deterministic. Filed as GH #169 (confirmed_bug).

Two bignum cases show a 45-digit JSON integer literal (beyond u64::MAX) silently accepted and downgraded to a lossy f64 (999999999999999999999999999999999999999999 → 999999999999999900000000000000000000000000.0) with no diagnostic. serde_json falls back to an f64 visit for out-of-range integers; no magnitude/precision guard exists on the JSON path (unlike the existing YAML NaN/Infinity guard). Filed as GH #170 (inconclusive, needs a documented numeric-fidelity decision).

The other 16 cases (nested/jagged JSON+YAML at moderate depth, empty values, numeric edges, mixed-type arrays) all passed or were correct intentional boundaries.

Full evidence, exact minimized template/input, and root-cause/recommended-fix detail: see the companion panel.
sections.context_text: Fuzz session qa-fuzz-20260729-0002, worker shape-probe (target: var-file, seed 261). 20 bounded JSON/YAML var-file cases. 16/20 passed (including 16 other nested/jagged JSON+YAML at moderate depth, empty values, numeric edges, mixed-type arrays -- all correct/intentional-boundary). 2 cases (depth 8000 and 16000) showed quadratic O(depth^2) latency before ERR_CONFIG_PARSE (recursion limit exceeded) fires -- filed as GH #169, confirmed_bug, reproduced 3/3. 2 cases exercised a 45-digit JSON integer literal beyond u64::MAX, silently downgraded to a lossy f64 with no diagnostic -- filed as GH #170, inconclusive pending a numeric-fidelity decision.

findings.command: cargo run -p sc-compose -- render --template min.j2 --var-file deep-depth-N.yaml
findings.observed_result: Wall time before ERR_CONFIG_PARSE (recursion limit exceeded): depth 500=0.011s, 1000=0.019s, 2000=0.055s, 4000=0.190s, 8000=0.697s, 16000=2.653s, 50000=~25.6s -- quadratic O(depth^2) scaling
findings.expected_oracle: recursion-limit rejection should be bounded/near-linear in nesting depth, not quadratic
findings.requirement_trace: No requirement or ADR currently covers this behavior.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Create/update an NFR capping var-file ingestion latency before recursion-limit rejection; this is a genuine performance gap, not intentionally unsupported.
findings.root_cause: crates/sc-compose/src/var_file.rs::parse_var_file_contents serde_yaml fallback path re-walks nested structure quadratically in depth before the recursion-limit check fires.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the recursion-depth check to a single top-down pass, or replace the serde_yaml fallback with an iterative depth-tracked parser so depth-N rejection stays near O(N).

findings.command: cargo run -p sc-compose -- render --template min.j2 --var-file bignum.json
findings.observed_result: Exit 0; value silently rendered as 999999999999999900000000000000000000000000.0 (lossy f64 downgrade of a 45-digit integer), no diagnostic
findings.expected_oracle: exact-precision preservation, or an explicit numeric-fidelity diagnostic when a JSON integer literal exceeds u64::MAX
findings.requirement_trace: No requirement or ADR currently covers this behavior.
findings.requirement_follow_up: Named decision owner needed (team-lead/comp) to decide reject/warn/arbitrary-precision handling for out-of-u64-range JSON integers; document the choice as an ADR once decided.
findings.root_cause: serde_json falls back to an f64 visit for JSON integers outside u64::MAX range; no magnitude/precision guard exists on the JSON var-file ingestion path (unlike the existing YAML NaN/Infinity guard).
findings.recommended_fix: Add a JSON numeric-fidelity guard mirroring the YAML NaN/Infinity guard; file an ADR recording the chosen behavior.

sections.title: Worker: template-probe
sections.summary: 15/20 passed. GH #167 confirmed_bug reconfirmed (loop.* misclassified as undeclared under --strict) -- not new, out of scope for PR #165. 1 not_a_bug note (minijinja has no .items() method).
sections.body_html:
Target: renderer · Seed 261 · Iterations 20 · Passed 15 · Failed 5 · Result FAIL.

4 of the 5 failed cases were intentional-boundary negative-contract rejections (include-cycle, include path-traversal escape, malformed custom-delimiter template, oversized nesting depth) and 1 was a self-corrected test-authoring error -- not product findings.

loop.index/loop.last are misclassified as undeclared under --strict, reproducing in the simplest single-loop template, 3/3 deterministic. This reconfirms already-filed GH #167 from a prior campaign; it is out of scope for PR #165 and was not re-filed.

A dict-.items()-method case is not_a_bug: minijinja has no Python-style .items() method; the |items filter and bare for k in dict both verified working correctly with Unicode keys.

Nested loops (3 levels, jagged/empty arrays), conditionals/elif chains, includes (single/multi-level), custom delimiters, whitespace control, Unicode values/keys, and default()/missing-field handling all passed correctly.

Full evidence, exact minimized template/input, and root-cause/recommended-fix detail: see the companion panel.
sections.context_text: Fuzz session qa-fuzz-20260729-0002, worker template-probe (target: renderer, seed 261). 20 bounded Jinja rendering cases. 15/20 passed cleanly. Nested loops (3 levels, jagged/empty arrays), conditionals/elif chains, includes (single/multi-level, missing-file and path-traversal correctly rejected), custom delimiters, whitespace control, Unicode values/keys, and default()/missing-field handling all passed correctly. Of the 5 flagged: 4 were intentional boundaries (correct negative-contract rejections) and 1 was a self-corrected test-authoring error. 1 confirmed_bug finding: loop.index/loop.last misclassified as undeclared under --strict -- this reconfirms already-filed GH #167 (out of scope for PR #165, not re-filed). 1 not_a_bug note: minijinja has no .items() method; |items filter and bare for-in both verified working with Unicode keys.

findings.duplicate_of: GH #167 (already filed from a prior campaign, out of scope for PR #165, not re-filed)
findings.command: cargo run -p sc-compose -- render --strict --template min-loop.j2 --var-file items.json
findings.minimal_template: {% for x in items %}{{ loop.index }}:{{ x }}{% if loop.last %} (last){% endif %}{% endfor %}
findings.observed_result: --strict flags loop.index/loop.last as undeclared referenced tokens, causing a hard validation/render failure; reproduces in the simplest single-loop template, 3/3 deterministic
findings.expected_oracle: loop.* is a standard Jinja/minijinja builtin context object populated inside for-loops and must not be treated as an undeclared user variable under --strict
findings.requirement_trace: Already tracked as GH #167 (filed from a prior campaign); out of scope for PR #165.
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new requirement/ADR needed this round -- duplicate of an already-triaged, already-filed issue; defer to the existing GH #167 owner.
findings.root_cause: Strict-mode undeclared-variable validation walks referenced identifiers without special-casing the loop.* builtin namespace injected by minijinja at render time.
findings.recommended_fix: Exempt the loop.* builtin namespace from strict undeclared-variable checks in the validation pass (tracked under GH #167, not part of this PR's scope).

findings.command: cargo run -p sc-compose -- render --template dict-items.j2 --var-file unicode-dict.json
findings.minimal_template: {% for k in mydict %}{{ k }}{% endfor %} vs {% for k in mydict.items() %}{{ k }}{% endfor %}
findings.observed_result: minijinja has no Python-style .items() method (render error); the |items filter and bare for k in dict both verified working correctly with Unicode keys
findings.expected_oracle: not_a_bug -- .items() is not part of the documented minijinja surface; correct alternatives already work
findings.requirement_trace: minijinja intentionally does not implement Python's dict.items() method; this is a documented engine-surface boundary, not a gap.
findings.requirement_follow_up: No new documentation needed -- behavior is intentionally unsupported and correct alternatives (|items filter, bare for-in) already work.
findings.root_cause: n/a (engine-surface difference from Python, not a defect)
findings.recommended_fix: None required; optionally note the .items() vs |items distinction in user-facing template-authoring docs.

sections.title: Worker: boundary-probe
sections.summary: 29/29 passed. 0 unexpected failures. Two non-blocking notes recorded in report text (not filed as new GH issues): an undocumented --var-file/--var precedence rule, and a reconfirmation that GH #168 is still present.
sections.body_html:
Target: cli · Seed 261 · Iterations 29 · Passed 29 · Failed 0 · Result PASS -- all negative-contract cases produced stable diagnostics as designed.

FUZZ-B01 (non-blocking documentation-gap note, not filed as a GH issue this round): --var-file silently overrides a same-key --var flag (last-loaded-wins), matching deterministic code behavior in crates/sc-compose/src/render_request.rs:267-274, undocumented in docs/requirements.md FR-2. Not a bug, but worth documenting.

FUZZ-B02 (not_a_bug): GH #168 (var-file path confinement gap) reconfirmed still present at baseline 749a3e0; not re-filed, already tracked.

All other cases (non-object top-level values, malformed-but-YAML-valid JSON, duplicate keys, invalid var names, missing files, YAML anchors/aliases, dangerous-but-inert YAML tags, multi-var-file precedence) produced correct stable diagnostics (ERR_CONFIG_VARFILE/ERR_CONFIG_PARSE, exit 3), no panics/hangs.
